title: 1905: Bengal Divided, Swadeshi Born

endcard.line: Pictures: The Sphere, 1906; Lala Deen Dayal (public domain)

anim.title: July 1905
items: Bengal will be split in two
'Too large to govern', said the British

segments.say: In nineteen-oh-five, the Viceroy, Lord Curzon, announced that Bengal would be cut in two. Officially, it was too large to govern.
But Indians saw the real aim: to weaken Bengal, the centre of the national movement, by dividing it.

right.title: Bengal (west)
items: Hindu majority, with Bihar and Orissa

segments.say: The east, with Assam, would have a Muslim majority. The west, with Bihar and Orissa, a Hindu one. Many saw it as divide and rule.

items.text: Partition takes effect: a day of mourning
Foreign cloth burnt; Indian goods, schools, banks

segments.say: The answer was Swadeshi: buy Indian, boycott British goods. On the day partition took effect, the sixteenth of October, Bengal fasted and mourned.
Huge meetings like this one, in nineteen-oh-six, filled the streets. Rabindranath Tagore led people in tying rakhis on each other, as a sign of unity.

anim.title: What it changed
items: Mass protest beyond the educated few
Indian industry: mills, banks, soap, matches

segments.say: Swadeshi took the movement beyond the educated few, and sparked Indian mills, banks and national schools. 'Bande Mataram' became its slogan.
In nineteen eleven, the partition was undone. For GS One: Curzon's partition, the Swadeshi movement, and its reversal in nineteen eleven.
